messages.content: I need to start putting together our New York school-break trip. It will be the three of us, Friday, March 13 through Wednesday, March 18. My daughter cannot leave school early Friday, so we need to depart Dallas after 5:30 p.m. We already have a Saturday 2:00 p.m. matinee near Times Square and a youth-arts program at Lincoln Center Tuesday at 10:00 a.m.

I can compare the trip as a whole rather than treating the cheapest airfare and hotel separately. Are you flying from DFW, and what room setup and Wednesday arrival time in Dallas would work? Also, should I include checked luggage and airport transfers in the totals?

DFW. We need either two beds or a real bed plus a sleeper sofa; one bed for all three is not workable. Wednesday can be fairly flexible, but I do not want to land after 9:00 p.m. because she has school Thursday. Include one checked suitcase, and compare the airport transfers too.

Understood. I will price nonstop evening departures from DFW after 5:30 p.m., Wednesday returns arriving by 9:00 p.m., one checked bag, and Manhattan hotels with a valid three-person room. I will focus on LGA and EWR first because JFK is less convenient for your two scheduled locations unless its fare is materially better. Do you have a working ceiling for flights, hotel, and transfers together?
Try to keep those pieces near $4,000 total. I can go a little above that if the schedule and room are clearly better. The matinee is on West 45th Street, if that helps.

It does. The best flight snapshots are: LGA nonstop leaving DFW Friday at 6:35 p.m. and arriving 11:02 p.m., then leaving LGA Wednesday at 5:10 p.m. and reaching DFW at 8:15 p.m., for $447 per person. EWR has a nonstop at 6:55 p.m.-11:28 p.m. and a Wednesday return at 4:40 p.m.-7:48 p.m. for $398 per person. The lowest workable JFK itinerary is $426 per person but arrives at 12:06 a.m. Friday night, so I would drop it. These are current economy totals with carry-ons; one shared checked suitcase adds about $80 round trip.
The LGA times seem better. Is EWR actually enough cheaper to justify getting into Manhattan that late?

Probably not by much. The airfare difference for three is $147. A taxi or app car from LGA to Midtown late Friday and back Wednesday should run about $120-$160 total including tolls and tips. From EWR, two car transfers are more likely $190-$250 total. Using midpoint estimates, EWR gives back roughly $80 of its airfare advantage in transfers, leaving only about $67 in net savings. The EWR ride can also take 45-75 minutes at those hours, while LGA to Midtown is commonly 25-50 minutes. Train service from EWR would lower the cost, but after an 11:28 p.m. arrival it adds transfers and walking with luggage.
Then keep LGA as the leading flight. Show me hotels where we will not discover at check-in that the second bed was only a request.

I found two bookable room types that explicitly sleep three. The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central has two queen beds and totals $2,293.40 for five nights, including estimated taxes and its mandatory destination charge. It is about a 7-minute walk to the West 45th Street theater and roughly 15 minutes to Lincoln Center by subway. The Riu Plaza New York Times Square has two full beds, breakfast for three included, and totals $2,486.75 including taxes and mandatory charges. It is about a 4-minute walk to the theater and 12-18 minutes to Lincoln Center by subway or bus.
How different are the rooms? Two full beds may be tight, but breakfast for three in Manhattan has value.

The Hilton room is the stronger physical setup: two queens, approximately 300 square feet, a mini-fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. The Riu room is closer to 250 square feet with two full beds, a mini-fridge, and no microwave; breakfast is included, but the room will feel tighter with three people and luggage. At the Hilton, a simple nearby breakfast for three could add roughly $45-$65 per day. Even three hotel breakfasts would erase most of the $193.35 room-price difference.
Does either total hide a resort fee or something payable later? And can we cancel?

The quoted totals include the mandatory charges shown in the current rate breakdown. Hilton's total includes a $30 nightly destination charge plus tax; it is collected with the room balance, not an extra amount beyond $2,293.40. The rate can be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Eastern on March 10. Riu's $2,486.75 total includes its listed facility charge and taxes, with free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on March 9. Incidental holds and optional purchases are separate at both properties.
Give me the full combinations, including the suitcase and realistic transfers. Add subway costs too so I can compare honestly.

Using $140 for round-trip LGA taxis, $220 for round-trip EWR cars, the $80 checked suitcase, and $102 for three seven-day OMNY fare caps, the estimates are: LGA plus Hilton, $3,956.40; LGA plus Riu, $4,149.75; EWR plus Hilton, $3,889.40; EWR plus Riu, $4,082.75. Those totals include airfare for three, the five-night hotel with mandatory taxes and fees, one checked bag, airport transfers, and local subway or bus rides. Meals, activities, and optional hotel incidentals are not included.
So the EWR-Hilton combination saves only $67 against LGA-Hilton, correct?

Correct: $3,889.40 versus $3,956.40 on the midpoint estimates. Transfer pricing can easily move by $30-$50, so that $67 is not a dependable saving. LGA also gets you to the hotel earlier Friday and gives you 27 more minutes before the Wednesday flight while still landing in Dallas before 8:30 p.m.
What time would we need to leave Manhattan Wednesday for each airport? I do not want the last day swallowed by airport logistics.

For the 5:10 p.m. LGA flight, I would leave Midtown around 2:15 p.m., targeting arrival near 3:15 p.m. For the 4:40 p.m. EWR flight, I would leave around 1:15 p.m., targeting 2:30 p.m. because the Hudson crossing is less predictable. The LGA schedule preserves about an extra hour in Manhattan and has a slightly later hotel departure.

That settles the airport. Keep the 6:35 Friday DFW-LGA and the 5:10 Wednesday LGA-DFW. Before narrowing the hotels, tell me whether the Hilton location will be annoyingly crowded compared with the Riu.

Both are in the Times Square theater district, so neither is a quiet-neighborhood choice. The Hilton is on West 42nd Street near Broadway and has heavier pedestrian traffic immediately outside, especially Friday and Saturday evening. The Riu is on West 46th Street west of Eighth Avenue, where the block is somewhat less intense while remaining close to your theater. For Lincoln Center, both involve a short ride; the Hilton has slightly easier access to multiple subway lines, while the Riu offers the shorter walk to the matinee.

Keep both. The Hilton wins on beds and total price; the Riu wins on breakfast and being a little removed from the busiest part. Are there any room-category details I need to preserve when we come back to book?

Yes. For the Hilton, retain the room labeled exactly “Two Queen Beds,” occupancy three; do not substitute a king room with a rollaway request. For the Riu, retain “Deluxe Two Full Beds,” also showing occupancy three and breakfast included for all registered guests. In either case, verify the final page still shows five nights, three guests, all mandatory charges, and the stated cancellation deadline before payment.
Good. Do not book anything today. Leave me with the flight schedule, the two hotel candidates, and the totals we should use for the decision.

The leading flights are the nonstop DFW-LGA itinerary: Friday, March 13, 6:35 p.m.-11:02 p.m., returning Wednesday, March 18, 5:10 p.m.-8:15 p.m. Airfare is currently $1,341 for three, plus about $80 for one checked suitcase. Candidate one is Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central, Two Queen Beds, $2,293.40 for five nights; the complete working trip total is $3,956.40. Candidate two is Riu Plaza New York Times Square, Deluxe Two Full Beds with breakfast for three, $2,486.75; its complete working total is $4,149.75. Both totals include estimated LGA taxis and three OMNY fare caps. Nothing has been booked, and prices and inventory need to be refreshed before purchase.
